dedupe_keys.name: drought gov standardized drought indices data download climate engine

description: Daily updated drought index maps for the United States in GIS-ready form. The Drought.gov page says the site runs an operational Climate Engine API, built on Google Earth Engine and the NOAA Open Data Dissemination programme, to produce hundreds of drought indices each day from NOAA, NASA and partner datasets, standardised to the 1991-2020 reference period, including percent of normal precipitation, SPI, SPEI and EDDI, and that they are free as GeoTIFF downloads and XYZ map tiles (zoom 1 to 5), with partner data from NOAA NCEI. Coverage is the United States. Caveats: the licence is not stated on the page read, and tiles exist only for coarse zoom levels. For simulation it gives current and recent drought conditions to drive crop, water supply, wildfire and river transport impact models. A related catalogue record is the SPEI-HR global drought indices.
